title: Kamishiro Rui — To The Undersea Show!〔Part1〕Side Story (Part 1)

rows.Line: Morinomiya Music Academy - Rehearsal Room

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: Heh heh heh... We finally get to have our first lesson at Morinomiya!

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: The revue has a storied history dating back over a hundred years, and we get to study at its school.

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: I've never been this excited in my life!!

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line:
Me neither.
We've been given quite an extraordinary opportunity here.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: This is arguably the best place to learn about musicals, so we'll need to make the most of our time here.

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: Agreed! However...

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: Hm? Is something wrong?

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: I'm a little worried about Nene and Emu.

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: We get to attend classes with the rest of the boys together, but Nene and Emu have been sent to study with the girls and operations team respectively.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: Right. We haven't been separated like this before now...

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: But I don't think we need to worry about them.

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: Hm? What makes you say that?

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: Nene and Emu have both overcome quite a lot in order to get to this point.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: They both know how to turn their worry and anxiety into fuel for moving forward.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: If anything, they may grow quite a bit while they're away from us.

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line:
Good point...
Then, we'll also need to do our very best.

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line:
Starting with our first lesson!
Let's go and give it everything we have, Rui!

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: Yes, let's improve so much that even they won't believe it.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line:
(Our first lesson involves ballet.
We're beginning with warm-up stretches and barre work.)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (Place one leg on the barre and tilt your upper body forwards, backwards and side to side. This is an exercise called “limbering”, intended to make your groin more flexible.)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: Keep your leg in this position and tilt your upper body...!

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line:
H-Hnnggg...!
Is this supposed to be this hard...?!

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: Professional ballet dancers can do this with ease. I have nothing but respect for them...!

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (The other students are also having no trouble doing this.)

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: (Which means this is a basic exercise to them. In that case...)

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: Rui?! You can keep going, right?!

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: Of course...!

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: *Wince*

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: Aaarrrghhh...!!!
After the lesson

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: Flexibility is my biggest foe at this point...

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: The same goes for me...

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: However, we seem to be doing okay in terms of stamina.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line:
Yes...
Our Mikazukigumi training seems to be paying off.

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line:
That is nice to know...
But does this mean we're going to be shouting in pain during every ballet lesson?

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: If we don't find a way to become much more flexible very fast, then yes.

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: What if we started drinking a liter of vinegar a day, starting now...?

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: I'm not sure even your stomach can handle that, Tsukasa.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: Also, what you said is just an old wives' tale. There's no scientific evidence that drinking vinegar makes one more flexible.

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: Ah, that's unfortunate...

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line:
However, well...
It could be fun to run an experiment to see if bathing in vinegar can help us become more flexible.

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: Bathing in vinegar?

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: Vinegar helps cuts of meat become softer by causing the protein within to denature, yes?

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: So, what if the same applied to our bodies♪

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: Yes, because it would make us softer... No, wait! That only works when you're cooking meat!

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: Yes, but cooking is based in science.

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line:
Still!
Instead of making us more flexible, we'd essentially be prepping ourselves for the grill!

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line:
Unfortunately, you're right.
Which means we'll have to keep searching for another way to become more flexible...

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: Yes... Unfortunately...

rows.Speaker: Rui & Tsukasa
rows.Line: *Sigh*
